name: last_30_min_momentum_5s
author: adapted from claude_strategist
thesis: Stocks that are up/down > 1% for the day with sustained volume tend to accelerate in the last 30 minutes (14:45-15:15) as institutional portfolio managers who have been monitoring all day make final positioning decisions. The 'last call' effect creates a rush to participate. Edge persists because the timing is structural — fund managers have end-of-day NAV and reporting constraints that create this flow pattern.
mechanism: The final 30 minutes see concentrated institutional flow as fund managers rebalance positions and mark-to-market. Options market makers adjust delta hedges ahead of close, creating predictable directional pressure. The increasing urgency to execute before close amplifies any existing directional bias.

indicators.name: day_return
indicators.purpose: how much stock has moved today

weaknesses: Short hold time (44 bars max) limits profit potential per trade
On reversal days, the last 30 min go against the day's trend — stop loss triggered
Screening for 1%+ movers at 14:45 biases toward momentum stocks that may be overextended
prior_art: Last-hour momentum — well-documented in market microstructure (Bogousslavsky 2016)
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
